assumptions: The input did not provide a structured state list, so the twelve state names and several capacity partitions were inferred from the NL obligations rather than copied from SpecJson.

The model is a guard-selected condition-classification abstraction: each cycle can reselect the active dispatch state from current PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity variables rather than preserving additional mode memory.
eng3_Pmax is interpreted as the LNG engine capacity; Pd1max and Pd2max are interpreted as DG1 and DG2 capacity bounds.
Pbat_Pmax is introduced as the battery discharge capacity bound because the NL requires battery discharge decisions but does not name the bound.
Requested generator power is modeled as aggregate Pg_req plus unit cut-in flags, not separate per-generator dispatch setpoints.
Load cut-in/cut-out commands are represented as aggregate cmd_load_cutin and cmd_load_cutout flags because the NL does not list individual load classes or shedding thresholds.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
Dispatch follows priority: LNG before diesel units.
FSM returns requested generator power and battery discharge power when demand exceeds renewable generation.

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init: with default PL=0 and SoC below 0.95, EMS initializes/selects zero-load battery charging from available RES.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_charge

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at the SoC=0.95 boundary with PL=0, RES production should go to spare rather than battery charging.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_soc_full_spare_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when renewable power exceeds load and SoC is below 0.95, all load is RES-served and residual RES charges the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at SoC=0.95 with renewable power exceeding load, residual RES should be treated as spare power.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when RES is below load, SoC exactly 0.2 is suitable for battery use and deficit within battery capacity is discharged.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_at_low_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with SoC below 0.2, LNG should cover the RES deficit plus the Pgmax/5 charging margin when within LNG capacity.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC but battery capacity insufficient and LNG capacity enough, LNG alone should be cut in before diesel.
scenario_results.name: lng_only_when_battery_capacity_insufficient

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and deficit above LNG capacity but within LNG plus battery capacity, dispatch LNG and battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: lng_battery_when_deficit_exceeds_lng

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and deficit above LNG, LNG plus DG1 should include the Pd1max/10 charging margin when within capacity.
scenario_results.name: low_soc_lng_dg1_charge_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when deficit exceeds LNG and battery contribution is not enough, but fits LNG plus DG1, DG1 is cut in without DG2.
scenario_results.name: lng_dg1_without_battery_or_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when deficit exceeds LNG plus DG1 but is within LNG plus DG1 plus DG2, all thermal units including DG2 are cut in.
scenario_results.name: all_thermal_dg2_last_priority

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: for extreme demand beyond all RES and thermal resources, all thermal units are activated and remaining lack is covered by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: overload_battery_cover_extreme_demand

evidence: NL: "issuing cut-in and cut-out commands for generating units and loads"
DSL: every state's during action assigns cmd_load_cutin = 1 and cmd_load_cutout = 0
Variables include cmd_load_cutin and cmd_load_cutout, but no guards or actions distinguish load command cases
findings.summary: The DSL is broadly faithful to the NL dispatch policy and covers the twelve inferred operating states, but load cut-in/cut-out behavior is under-modeled: load cut-in is always 1 and load cutout is always 0, so the model does not meaningfully issue load shedding or restoration commands despite the NL naming load cut-in and cut-out commands.

evidence: GroundingMap.source_summary assumption: "Requested generator power is modeled as aggregate Pg_req plus unit cut-in flags, not separate per-generator dispatch setpoints."
DSL has cmd_LNG, cmd_DG1, cmd_DG2 and Pg_req, but no per-unit Pg_LNG_req, Pd1_req, or Pd2_req outputs
NL refers to generating units and cut-in/cut-out commands for generating units
findings.summary: The model uses aggregate generator power Pg_req plus Boolean unit commands, but does not decompose requested power by LNG, DG1, and DG2. This is an acceptable abstraction only if aggregate dispatch is intended; otherwise it can hide per-unit power allocation and cut-out semantics.

evidence: DSL uses global forced transitions: ! * -> state for all 12 operating cases

GroundingMap.source_summary assumption: "guard-selected condition-classification abstraction" and "rather than preserving additional mode memory"
findings.summary: The dispatch is implemented as a condition-classification table with instantaneous reselection from current inputs, rather than a temporal FSM with memory, hysteresis, or event-driven transitions. This may be sufficient for the stated logical partitioning, but it is a simplification of the NL phrase "dynamically switching states" across changing periods and operating conditions.

evidence: DSL: repeated ! * -> ZeroLoadCharge/ZeroLoadSpare/RESCoversCharge/.../OverloadBatteryCover transitions
inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_events = 0
inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.max_hierarchy_depth = 1
findings.summary: state_mode_decorative: the leaf states primarily label mutually exclusive guard regions and have no internal mode memory; all operating states are reachable through ! * reselection. This is advisory because the NL itself emphasizes logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal... state shall never occur in practice."
DSL: ! * -> OverloadBatteryCover : if [PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > eng3_Pmax + Pd1max + Pd2max]
DSL OverloadBatteryCover: Pbat_discharge = PL - Ppv - Pw - eng3_Pmax - Pd1max - Pd2max
OverloadBatteryCover guard does not include SoC >= 0.2 or Pbat_discharge <= Pbat_Pmax
findings.summary: The overload state is modeled as an executable dispatch state even though the NL calls it illegal and says it shall never occur in practice. The selected action also discharges the battery without checking SoC or Pbat_Pmax in that overload branch. This is not marked blocking because the NL explicitly describes all-thermal activation plus battery coverage for the illegal overload case, but it should be annotated or guarded as an exceptional/illegal state if the DSL supports that.
